text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the most likely next word in a sentence, based on patterns they have learned. During training, they study enormous amounts of text from books, websites and articles. To get good results, users need prompt engineering: writing clear and specific instructions helps the model give better answers. LLMs can write texts, translate languages, answer questions and summarise information quickly. However, they also have limits. They sometimes produce false information, cannot check facts on their own, and may reflect biases found in their training data. For these reasons, people should always review their output carefully.
